fr.elements: Main Building; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Landscaped Area; Open Terrain; Street Frontage; Pedestrian Walkways
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain unobstructed at all times could significantly improve emergency responder access and reduce response delays. Keeping the driveway clear of parked vehicles, equipment, or other obstructions would support simultaneous ingress and egress for emergency apparatus. Clearly marking the access point from the street frontage may assist responders in locating the entry under low-visibility or nighttime conditions. Given the limited rear access to the structures, communicating alternate foot-access pathways through the open terrain to local responders in advance could support tactical planning and personnel movement around the property during an emergency operation.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Fuel Continuity; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Scattered Trees; Vegetated Access Route; Limited Defensible Space; Brushland Interface; Heavy Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing brush and dense ground vegetation in the immediate zone surrounding the structure could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity near the building. Creating and maintaining separation between shrubs, tree clusters, and the structure may reduce the opportunity for fire to move directly toward improvements. Managing vegetation along the access route would support firefighter ingress and egress during a fire event, as well as resident evacuation. Where shrubs are located adjacent to the structure, increasing horizontal spacing between individual plants and between shrubs and combustible portions of the building could reduce fuel continuity. Thinning ground vegetation within the immediate structure perimeter and extending cleared or reduced-fuel zones outward where feasible would support suppression operations and improve overall wildfire resilience. Ongoing vegetation management across the mixed cover present on the property may help maintain these improvements over time.
